title: stats.spectral.compute_periodogram
---



```python
stats.spectral.compute_periodogram(
    y,
    *,
    max_peaks=5,
    scaling='spectrum',
    fs=None,
)
```

Compute the periodogram of a time series.

Wraps `scipy.signal.periodogram` with a ``boxcar`` window to match
the reference implementation.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                              | Description                                                                                             | Default      |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|
| y         | [pd](`pandas`).[Series](`pandas.Series`)          | Series to analyse.  Must be a non-empty pandas Series without missing values (validated via `check_y`). | _required_   |
| max_peaks | [int](`int`)                                      | Number of top peaks to surface.                                                                         | `5`          |
| scaling   | [str](`str`)                                      | Spectrum scaling forwarded to ``scipy``.                                                                | `'spectrum'` |
| fs        | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[float](`float`)\] | Sampling frequency.  Defaults to ``1.0`` (cycles per sample).                                           | `None`       |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                       | Description                                          |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [PeriodogramResult](`spotforecast2_safe.stats.spectral.PeriodogramResult`) | A `PeriodogramResult` with the full spectrum and the |
|        | [PeriodogramResult](`spotforecast2_safe.stats.spectral.PeriodogramResult`) | top-``max_peaks`` periods.                           |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                       |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If ``y`` is not a pandas Series.  |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If ``y`` contains missing values. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#777327cf .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from spotforecast2_safe.stats.spectral import compute_periodogram

t = np.arange(512)
y = pd.Series(np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / 32))
result = compute_periodogram(y, max_peaks=1)
print(int(round(result.top_periods.index[0])))
```
